Project: toxval

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides project-specific context only — repo structure, dependencies, analysis decisions, and prompt logging. It does not impose personal style preferences on collaborators.

For Claude: If a CLAUDE.md exists in the parent directory of this repo, read it before proceeding — it may contain user-specific environment and style preferences. If no such file exists, apply sensible R defaults and ask if anything is unclear. This repo-level file takes precedence over any parent-level file where they conflict.

1. Repo Type

R package — standard usethis/devtools structure, R CMD check via GitHub Actions, pkgdown site, testthat, roxygen2.

2. What This Repo Does

The toxval R package extracts toxicity threshold estimates — No-Significant-Effect Concentrations (NSECs) and ECx values — from fitted concentration–response models. It addresses the challenge of deriving these endpoints consistently across modelling frameworks.

It currently supports Bayesian models fitted with brms (ecx(), nsec(), and nsec_multi() for multivariate fits) and frequentist models fitted with drc (nsec() only). toxval_predict() returns the predictions of a brms or drc fit over a grid of x values; phase 4 of the refactor (REFACTOR-human.md) rebuilds the metrics on it. Models fitted with bayesnec are handled by toxval_predict() methods in toxval, with bayesnec in Suggests (T35).

bayesnec keeps its own ecx(), nsec() and ecnsec(). RF develops both packages and keeps their results in agreement (T42). A change here that alters a value returned for a bayesnecfit or bayesmanecfit, or by nsec() for a brmsfit or drc fit, is compared with bayesnec under matching options before it merges. Record the result, and whether bayesnec is to follow, on a bayesnec issue. A change that leaves every returned value unchanged needs neither. Both packages export ecx() and nsec(), and the one attached last masks the other without a warning, so with both attached call each with its package prefix.

Key inputs are fitted model objects, and the primary outputs are standardised toxicity metrics (e.g. NSEC, EC10, EC50) that can be used in environmental risk assessment or guideline derivation.

3. Package Dependencies in Scope

Dependencies are defined in DESCRIPTION (Imports + Suggests). Read that file to determine what is available.

4. Key Files and Structure

R package layout

R/              # exported functions — one file per logical group
tests/testthat/ # testthat test files (test-<name>.R); fixtures/ holds stored fits and data
tests/local/    # slower tests run by hand, not by R CMD check; skipped without bayesnec
man/            # auto-generated by roxygen2, do not edit manually
data-raw/       # scripts that produce the fixtures in tests/testthat/fixtures/
vignettes/      # long-form documentation, as Quarto vignettes
DESCRIPTION     # package metadata, imports, suggests
NEWS.md         # changelog, generated by fledge — do not edit by hand
prompts/        # session prompt logs (see Section 6)

5. Git Workflow

This repo uses a standard open-source fork workflow:

upstream (open-AIMS/toxval) → origin (beckyfisher/toxval fork) → local workspace
  • upstream (open-AIMS/toxval) — the authoritative project repo. Never push directly; contribute only via pull requests from the fork.
  • origin (beckyfisher/toxval) — the personal fork on GitHub. Positron’s Source Control sync (↑↓) pushes/pulls against this remote.
  • main is the integration branch in both repos. New work branches off main; PRs go from beckyfisher/toxval into open-AIMS/toxval.

Keeping main up to date with upstream

Set the local main to track upstream/main, so a pull follows the authoritative repo rather than the fork:

git branch -u upstream/main main

Then, before starting any new feature branch:

git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge --ff-only upstream/main
git push origin main

6. Prompt Log

Session logs for this project are in prompts/. Create the folder if it does not exist. Use a short kebab-case descriptor as the filename for each session (e.g. bayesian-model-refactor.md). If a file with that name already exists, append to it.

Log format for each session entry:

## Session: <descriptor>
Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
Model: <model name and version>

### Prompts and Responses

**User:** <prompt text>

**Claude:** <summary of response — full code blocks where relevant, prose summarised>
